key_insight: A large-scale log of real-world interactions (200k+ queries) from two deployed LLM-powered research tools reveals how researchers actually discover literature and ask scientific questions, exposing common query types, engagement patterns, and opportunities to improve tool design.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of empirical, real-world data on how researchers use AI-powered scientific tools, enabling evidence-based improvements to interfaces, retrieval strategies, and evaluation metrics.
method: Collected and anonymized interaction logs and user queries from two deployed tools (literature discovery and scientific Q&A) within an LLM-based retrieval-augmented generation platform.
Performed exploratory analyses of query types, session/engagement metrics, and feature usage to characterize researcher behavior at scale.
Derived design-relevant insights and usage patterns to inform benchmarking, UX adjustments, and future research tool development.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners and tool builders with a grounded dataset and behavioral findings to guide better evaluation, UI design, retrieval/LLM integration, and deployment decisions for scientific research tools.
visual_elements: Overview diagram of the deployed platform (RAG backbone + two interfaces) showing data flow from query → retrieval → LLM response
Stacked bar or pie chart of query types (e.g., discovery, factual Q&A, methods-focused) to show distribution
Funnel or session timeline visual showing engagement metrics (queries per session, follow-ups, abandonment)
Heatmap or timeline of feature usage and response satisfaction to highlight when/where users engage most
paper_title: Understanding Usage and Engagement in AI-Powered Scientific Research Tools: The Asta Interaction Dataset
paper_authors: Dany Haddad, Dan Bareket, Joseph Chee Chang, Jay DeYoung, Jena D. Hwang
